spec.reason: Ranked first because cartservice is a single replica, has high risk, is shared by frontend and checkoutservice, and reaches all five flows. Prior cartservice pod kills affected all flows with peak errors near 90–100% and recovery around 22–31 seconds, making this the broadest shopper-visible test.
spec.hypothesis: The killed cartservice pod will cause visible errors across shopping and checkout flows until Kubernetes replaces it; recovery will take tens of seconds. The brief outage is expected to complete rather than be stopped by the guard, consistent with prior cartservice pod-kill runs.

spec.reason: Ranked second because paymentservice is a single replica on the revenue-critical checkout path, but its reach is limited to checkout. Prior 30-second paymentservice failures affected checkout; observed peak error rates around 21% show this failure is visible and may activate the guard.
spec.hypothesis: With paymentservice unavailable, checkout attempts will fail while the other flows remain usable. Errors should dominate rather than latency; the guard is likely to abort if the checkout error threshold is exceeded on consecutive checks.

decisions.reason: The cartservice pod kill completed as predicted and affected all five flows, with 90.48% impact error rate, a 28.21× worst-flow slowdown, and 27.6 s recovery; the shop is now healthy. The planned 30 s paymentservice pod_failure is validator-approved and probes the distinct, checkout-limited failure mode.

The paymentservice pod_failure aborted at a 25% peak error rate, with 75% checkout errors; unexpectedly, add_to_cart also reached 729.2 ms p95 (110.48× baseline) despite zero errors. Probe paymentservice with a moderate delay to see whether a less disruptive fault reproduces latency or cross-flow impact.
